text.en:
Dev had two bar magnets. When he brought two ends close, they pulled together with a click. When he turned one around, they pushed apart.
"They are playing push and pull!" he laughed.
His sister said, "Each end is a pole, and poles have rules."

Every magnet has two poles, a north pole and a south pole. The pull is strongest at the poles.
Unlike poles attract each other: north and south pull together. Like poles repel each other: north with north, or south with south, push apart.
A magnet hung freely turns to point north and south, which is why a compass works. Magnets are used in fridge doors, speakers, toys, cranes that lift scrap iron and in compasses.

problem.en: What happens if you bring the north pole of one magnet near the north pole of another?

text.en: Both are the same kind of pole, so they are like poles.

why.en: North and north are like poles.

text.en: So the two magnets push away from each other.

prompt.en: A friend says a magnet attracts everything it touches. How will you correct this?

requiredIdeas.en: A magnet attracts only magnetic things like iron.
Two like poles even push each other away.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking a magnet pulls all materials.

points.en: A magnet has a north pole and a south pole.
Unlike poles attract and like poles repel.
Compasses, fridge doors and cranes use magnets.
